page: Amazon Web Services m5n.large is an entry-level general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The server provides 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core on a dedicated Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. Memory is provisioned at 8.0 GB of DDR4 running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI support, AES cryptography acceleration, and BMI2 instructions. The instance includes no integrated local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistence, and features a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations position the m5n.large in entry-tier performance brackets across general compute and memory tasks. The instance scored 1101.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1306.0 in multi-core metrics, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 1993.27. Memory throughput reaches 13.27 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 11.41 GB/sec for writes. Application-specific benchmarks reflect 1.66 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 1.86 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, while lightweight language model inference achieved 32.9 tokens per second on a small 135M model.

Because computing capacity is limited to one physical core hyperthreaded to two logical execution contexts, the instance exhibits constrained throughput during heavy concurrent execution. Cost efficiency is optimized for network-oriented workloads requiring Nitro-backed throughput rather than intensive computational pipelines. The configuration is primarily suitable for microservices, lightweight web servers, development environments, and auxiliary routing tasks requiring balanced memory without dedicated high-speed local disk requirements.
description: Amazon Web Services m5n.large is a general-purpose Nitro instance designed around a 2-vCPU, 1-physical-core Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz. Supported by 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory at 3 GHz, it delivers a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory allocation. The hardware platform includes AVX-512 with VNNI vector enhancements and AES cryptographic extensions. It operates without bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage, while maintaining a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. In benchmark tests, the instance scored 1101.0 in single-core Geekbench and 1306.0 in multi-core Geekbench, delivering 1.66 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.86 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. Given its two-thread limit and absence of local disk, the m5n.large serves cost-effectively for microservices, staging environments, API gateways, and low-traffic backend utilities.
